_about: Rolf, White Fest (141159, black_wolf_knight_wt23): translated from the game's Japanese, keeping his archaic knightly speech. Global names/terms: Rolf, Klaus, Helga, Magnos, Albert, Claw (Lord Navelle = Claudius Navelle), Nao Nagihara, the King of Dogfolk, dogfolk/catfolk, Whitetail, the Company of the Fang, Aegis, Tink, White Fest, Nimbus, Light. Own romanizations: Zahn (ツァーン), Gerda (ゲルダ), Paul (パウル), Lord Fang (ファング卿), Mordschlag (モルトシュラーク).
profile: A knight who has led the dogfolk to victory in countless battles. Having realized his own mistakes, he begins searching for a path he can truly believe in.
titleCondition: Level Rolf to 100 and obtain his Amity Scroll

speech.home/watashiwa_oto: I am the sword of the king, and of you all. And yet... I must face the mistakes I have long averted my eyes from.
speech.home/happihowaitofuesu_masaka: Happy White Fest. Never did I imagine I would be blessed with so many smiles. I am grateful for so rare an experience.
speech.home/saikinwa_shibuyano: Of late, I have been invited to Shibuya's board games. The rules are somewhat complex, but they share much with military strategy, and I find them surprisingly enjoyable. Would you care for a match?
speech.home/shirodononimo: One of these cookies for you as well, Sir Nimbus. This is no festival duty. Of my own will, I give them to those who have aided me. Will you accept it?
speech.home/chugio: Loyalty to the king. I long mistook that as all I was capable of. I shall wash away that shame by carving out a new path.
speech.home/shirokumasan: Polar Bear Cookies, is it. Perhaps they could be adopted as rations for the Company. With this flavor, they would be a joy for soldiers on the battlefield. Lion Cookies would serve as well, of course.
speech.ally/join: The knight Rolf Zahn, at your service. My attire is unusual, but fear not. This sword, and these cookies, I entrust to you.
speech.ally/evolution: Though this sword is stained with much blood, I swear once more to walk alongside you. From this moment on, I am my own sword, and yours.

1.title: Sweets or Knight
1.summary: Having lost sight of the path he once believed in, Rolf helps hand out sweets at Nimbus's suggestion. Dazzled by the sight of Palpebra's people laughing together regardless of race, Rolf recalls his wife's last words, and seeing his old acquaintances trying to change, begins searching for a new path.

lines.12: From this moment, Rolf Zahn once again takes command of the main army!
lines.15: To think those cats still had this much strength left. ...Lord Zahn. A royal command like this--
lines.18: No! Absolutely not! They chose to die on this very day rather than die tomorrow!
lines.21: ...If only the king had not chosen a war of annihilation... No, if only he had not kept you away from the front lines...!!
lines.24: ...We are the king's sword. A sword obeys only the will of the one who wields it.
lines.28: Now, soldiers! Follow me! Victory to the king!!
lines.40: Don't space out in the middle of the road. You've gotta be used to this place by now, right?
lines.44: How careless of me. It seems I was somewhat overwhelmed by the bustle, livelier than usual.
lines.47: Thinking gloomy thoughts again? That kind of stuff's--
lines.50: ...Well, while you're here. Why don't you help out a bit? Might take your mind off things.
lines.54: Polar Bear Cookies. To advertise the shop, I need you to hand these out to anyone and everyone.
lines.57: Understood. I shall undertake this duty with all my heart and soul.
lines.62: Ohhh? I told you to clean yourself up, but... You look the part...
lines.64: Never figured you'd have a sense of style. Didn't see that coming.
lines.68: These clothes were a gift from my wife.
lines.73: ...You were married!? Say that kinda thing sooner!!
lines.76: It was long ago. Illness took her, far before her time.
lines.83: Think nothing of it. You praised how they suit me. My wife must be pleased.
lines.86: Now then, Sir Klaus. In this operation, where lies my battlefield?
lines.90: Lord Zahn, you will lie in wait for anyone who passes through here. Meanwhile, I will push toward the market.
lines.94: As you command. May fortune favor you in battle.
lines.98: Free samples from that shop. May blessings be upon the future of so loving a pair.
lines.101: Children, take these. Should you like them, you may well beg the grown-ups for more.
lines.104: Drifters... laughing together, regardless of race. ...A fine town.
lines.108: ...Lord Zahn? Is that Lord Rolf Zahn?
lines.112: ...Lord Paul? And those with you... Why are dogfolk officers and soldiers in Palpebra?
lines.118: Classified, then. ...So the war is in motion.
lines.122: Mind going easy on the young ones? Mister Black Wolf.
lines.126: So this is what it means to poke a bush and find a snake. Quite the big catch.
lines.129: That's my line. I knew about Klaus, but I never expected you too.
lines.132: This is surprisingly enjoyable in its own way. Though I'm well aware it doesn't suit me.
lines.135: N-no!? It suits you very well... I mean, um!?
lines.138: There is no longer any need for formality. Now, how about a Polar Bear Cookie?
lines.144: ...It's been a long time. The last time we spoke alone like this was at my wife's funeral, I believe.
lines.147: Those clothes. Gerda picked them out, didn't she? I could tell right away.
lines.150: ...Gerda was a wonderful woman. Almost too dazzling for a little brat like me.
lines.154: ...She was a better wife than I deserved.
lines.157: I, who could not even be at her side when she passed...
lines.170: Ah, be cursed... be cursed... Cursed be this foolish man who weighed his wife's life against his soldiers'...!
lines.173: ...Lord Zahn. These are your lady wife's final words.
lines.178: "A path you can believe in..." was it.
lines.184: I didn't plan on saying anything about it after all this time. But--
lines.186: Those who couldn't go back to being soldiers. Those who could never become soldiers. ...They're trying to move forward.
lines.191: ...The answer already lies within. The enemy is within my own heart... is it.
lines.197: Hey. I heard. Sounds like you were a big hit.
lines.201: It was a rare experience. I thank you for your consideration.
lines.205: O-oh...? No idea what you mean, but good for you, I guess.
lines.209: Lovers whispering of love regardless of race. Little ones playing and laughing together.
lines.214: It made me realize that I too must change. ...Though how, I cannot yet see.
lines.222: I must thank Sir Klaus properly another day as well. He even gave me a gift, for my wife.
lines.225: Heh. Not bad. He's gotten pretty thoughtful...
lines.229: ...Sir Nimbus. Would you indulge me in some memories of my wife for a while?
lines.231: I am sure it would make a fine memorial.
lines.235: ......Fine, fine! If we can do it over drinks, I'm in.
lines.239: ...How many decades has it been. When I met her, I was still--

2.title: Warrior or Knight
2.summary: While Rolf hands out sweets to children in Shibuya, alarms ring out and monsters attack. Proposing a siege defense to keep the children safe, Rolf finds a new path in the fight to protect them, and resolves to do what he must as the king's sword.

lines.5: Happy White Fest! Children seeking sweets, assemble at once!
lines.8: The goods we hauled are right here. Quietly take your Polar Bear Cookies.
lines.14: With this, the request from the Mayor of Shibuya is complete. Well done, all.
lines.18: Great work, Rolf, Klaus! I'm so glad everyone was happy~.
lines.23: What of those children? They did not seem to be here earlier.
lines.27: Well... They're kind of a rowdy group, I guess...
lines.29: They're the type of kids who used to look up to Aegis... I bet it's awkward for them...
lines.33: Sir Klaus. Might you leave the remaining sweets to me?
lines.38: H-hey! What're you guys here for!
lines.40: Happy White Fest. I have come to hand out sweets to the children.
lines.43: Sweets...? A-are you stupid!? Don't treat us like little kids!
lines.45: All the more reason, then. The morale boost sweets bring is not to be underestimated. They are vital provisions even for strong soldiers.
lines.48: Eat these sweets and relax for a while. At times, laughing together with others is necessary too.
lines.54: This is... the Tinks' alarm!? Could monsters be in Shibuya--
lines.59: All of you, take shelter inside the building!!
lines.62: Sir Klaus, take the rear guard with me! Champion, please lead the children!!
lines.66: --Sorry to keep you waiting. I scouted the situation outside, if only briefly.
lines.68: It's the labyrinth after all. Monsters are pouring out from places connected underground, and there seems to be damage all over Shibuya.
lines.71: What, that's crazy bad! W-we gotta run...!!
lines.73: No. The surroundings are already a battlefield. A careless retreat would only invite danger.
lines.76: Champion. I propose we hold out in a siege.
lines.79: Right. With the children's safety in mind, that's best. Then I'll go call for help.
lines.81: I may not be much in a fight, but I can slip past the monsters' eyes.
lines.84: H-hey! We're not little kids either. We don't lose fights... Let us help with something!!
lines.87: ...With your aid, we are as good as ten thousand reinforcements. I shall rely on you fully.
lines.91: Now, prepare for the siege! Everyone, make haste!
lines.96: Hey, wolf mister! This is bad! Monsters got inside the building!
lines.102: ...B-bombs...!? Why do you even have those...!?
lines.104: Festival or not, one is never too prepared for war. Only natural for an officer.
lines.107: I-is it, though...? I'm glad the building didn't collapse...
lines.111: Destruction is a last resort. Rest assured.
lines.114: M-message! Monsters are coming in through the back door!!
lines.118: I leave this place to you, Sir Klaus!
lines.129: ......Heh. This exhilaration. I had long forgotten it. So this is what a battle without doubt feels like.
lines.136: Not a single one shall pass this place. Everyone, fall back to the next barricade!
lines.142: How incorrigible I am. Only with children in danger do I finally reach a knight's true calling.
lines.145: ...Gerda. You saw it all clearly, didn't you.
lines.149: Which is precisely why: Victory. Victory. Victory to all!!
lines.159: Phew~. I'm so glad everyone made it out safe~.
lines.162: We happened to run into the Champion. Thanks to that, we got here right away.
lines.166: Thank you for the rescue. But you are--
lines.170: We are the Company of the Fang. A gathering of soldiers with nowhere to belong.
lines.174: ...There is no way Palpebra would sit idle with a force this strong. Which means--
lines.178: Just like you guessed. We're in Palpebra because we're needed. That town's in danger.
lines.187: Why are you laughing at that!?
lines.191: Because I have found what I must become. I can see a path I can believe in.
lines.193: I too am a man who can only live in battle. And I kept fighting for the wrong reasons. But...
lines.197: You really are incorrigible. But I think you'll be fine now.
lines.200: Want to bare your fangs alongside ours? Sir Black Wolf Knight.
lines.205: Before I walk a path I can believe in, there is something I must do.

3.title: King or Knight
3.summary: Through Albert's arrangements, Rolf is granted an audience with the King of Dogfolk, and pleads to wield his strength to save Palpebra from danger. The king flies into a rage and rants senselessly, and Rolf finally parts ways with him, taking the new path he believes in as a guest commander of the Company of the Fang.

lines.5: My thanks to you, Lord Fang. Politics would never allow someone like me an audience with the king now.
lines.9: That's how small the king's influence has become. There's no need to thank me.
lines.11: But that man doesn't have the capacity to accept your feelings, Lord Zahn.
lines.15: ...Even so, I shall believe. In my king.
lines.19: Eh, just let him do what he wants. I think it's pointless too, though.
lines.24: ...Fine. But this will affect the lords as well. I'll at least be present.
lines.35: Rolf Zahn. I am grateful for this audience.
lines.39: ...It's been a long time. Show me the face you dare to come here with.
lines.43: Your Majesty. I have come today to present my petition.
lines.47: ...Very well. I shall hear the ravings of an ingrate.
lines.51: Yes, sire. At present, a town in a distant land stands on the brink of danger.
lines.54: I beg you, permit me to fight as the King's Sword to protect the people. All the people.
lines.61: That town is a miracle, where different races live together and laugh together.
lines.63: Under the king's name, we shall protect the people and atone for our sins.
lines.66: If the chance arises, I would like you to see that town someday, Your Majesty. And I humbly ask that your heart--
lines.75: I did good deeds, didn't I!!
lines.79: I! Drove off Whitetail! And made the dogfolk!! The conquerors!!
lines.82: If you had slaughtered every last one of those cats! I would never have ended up in this disgrace!!!
lines.86: ...Never... did I think he was this blind...!
lines.98: How dare you, you disloyal wretch...!!
lines.102: Displeased? But it's the truth! A truly loyal man would have stopped me with counsel long ago!!
lines.111: It's all your fault! There's no way I have any sins to atone for!!
lines.120: The sword I dedicated to you. I return it here.
lines.123: If it displeases you, then cut me down.
lines.133: Your Majesty. What you become is yours to choose.
lines.139: Y-y-you...! Putting on a face of loyalty now...!!
lines.143: Your worthless head! I'll cut it off, just as you wish!!
lines.148: ...The King's Sword seems to have been far too heavy for that man.
lines.152: My loyalty... These twenty-some years... Was it all... an illusion...
lines.160: I apologize for the wait. Thank you for your consideration.
lines.167: At this point, there is nothing left to discuss. ...Gerda knew everything.
lines.170: My foolishness in fleeing into battle without counseling the king, knowing the war was pointless.
lines.172: My foolishness in knowing of the coup plot, yet neither stopping it nor joining it.
lines.176: And she still stayed with you to the end, right? That's one hell of a woman.
lines.180: My pride and joy, a wife I never deserved.
lines.184: Lord Fang, Lord Navelle. Would you accept the sword of a fool such as this?
lines.188: Neither Claw nor I is a king. Isn't that right?
lines.193: We're comrades, dude! No need for all that stiff stuff!
lines.198: Besides, your new battlefield isn't here, is it?
lines.203: How careless of me. It seems habits ingrained to the bone don't come off easily.
lines.206: Gerda, this is farewell for a while. I may leave you lonely, but forgive me.
lines.210: ...Rest easy. I will not make the same mistake again.
lines.221: What a strange thing to say. I would never jest before a superior.
lines.223: New recruit, Rolf Zahn. I have fought on every front for twenty years. I am rather confident in handling gunpowder.
lines.229: That's what I mean! If that's not a joke, then what is it!!
lines.232: I heard that in the Company of the Fang, regardless of one's past, everyone starts over as a common soldier.
lines.237: Having you in line with the rest, Sir Black Wolf Knight, would make everyone else shrink back.
lines.240: You'll be treated as a guest commander. We're short on officers. I'm counting on you, okay?
lines.243: Understood. I shall fight with all my heart and soul. To protect that town.

1141159/1.19:
A knight who has led the dogfolk to victory
in countless battles. Having realized his own
mistakes, he begins searching for a path
he can truly believe in.

2000019/2.19:
"All for the future. The king's power is necessary," the two young men said, showing him a path of light.
But the king chose to drown in his obsession.
Shut away in the palace, he averts his eyes from everything, and has reportedly resolved that those who failed to stop his rampage are to blame.

Even so, many still seek to die for their loyalty.
They will always be called upon to question themselves.

5000628/1.19:
The late wife of Rolf, hailed as the strongest knight of the dogfolk.
On the battlefield by royal command, Rolf could not be at her side when she died, and regrets it still.
But her last words, from a woman who loved even that side of him, became the guidepost of Rolf's life.
In life, she was a dazzlingly bright and warm woman, and a good wife who always supported Rolf.

5000628/2.19:
Gerda often picked out Rolf's clothes for him, since he knew little about fashion.
Rolf remembers his wife's coordination, and still thinks back on it whenever he dresses himself.
His clothing is one of the bonds that tie him to his late wife, and being complimented on it fills him with pride in her, making him exceedingly happy.
